state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. In this case, you need to differentiate between rest and movement on a distance-time graph. Rest would be when the distance is not changing, while movement would be indicated by a change in distance over time.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so like... the flat bit in the middle is when Fido isn't moving because the distance stays the same, yeah? But I'm still confused about the bit that goes down - does that mean he's moving backwards towards his home, or is that something else?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: There is a specific procedure for this. Step 1 is to identify the operation; step 2 is to apply the rule for that operation. The downward sloping section on the graph indicates that Fido is moving back towards his home, as the distance is decreasing over time.

score.justification_pass2: The teacher consistently states explicit procedures (Step 1 and Step 2), provides clear rules for interpreting distance-time graphs, and gives direct corrective feedback on the student's misconception about the negative-sloping section, which is textbook rule-based instruction.
